full_judgment:
2. The facts of the case briefly are as follows: - 

 The petitioner-who claimed to be a citizen of Bangladesh and become the owner of the movable and immovable properties under the Will executed by his father late kalu Ram Behani and duly probated in Miscellaneous Case No. 11 of 1979 LAD in the Court of the District Judge, Bogra. While he was carrying on with his business at Bogra being of money entered into a contract with Benoy Kumar Ghose, son of Bepin Behari Ghose to sell .02 acre of land for a price of Tk. 15,000/- and thereafter executed a sale deed on 14.7.1991 on receipt of the price in cash. The said deed of sale was presented for registration on 16th July 1991 before the Sub-Registrar respondent No. 3 who by his order dated 16th July, 1991 refused to accept the same for registration with the endorsement that it was not accompanied by permission and/or no objection certificate of the Deputy Commissioner. Bogra as required under the provision of the Memo No. 320(19) - SW: Ma: (Ni-1) dated 10th June 1975 as communicated by the Deputy Commissioner, Bogra vide his Memo No. 602(5) dated 8-6-1975 and accordingly the deed was returned to the petitioner. 

 5. Mr. Md. Abdul Mannan Bhuiyan the learned Assistant Attorney General has appeared on behalf of the respondent No. 4 but no affidavit-in-opposition has been filed in the case. The learned Assistant Attorney General submitted that the memo issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs imposing restrictions are designed to prevents some underhand deals and also smuggling of money out of the country in consideration of the circumstances prevalent at the time but he admitted that this restriction cannot be treated as an absolute bar for transferring immovable property by the member of any community. The learned Assistant Attorney General then submitted that the memo only contained certain conditions for the parties to the transaction to comply but the petitioner having not fulfilled the said conditions, the respondent No. 3 had no alternative remedy but to refuse to accept the sale deed for registration. 

 8. It is not denied that the petitioner though belong to the Marwari Community is a citizen of Bangladesh and that he is the owner of the immovable property in the Bogra Town having the same inherited from his father. Now the question arises as to whether the petitioner being a citizen of the country owning property has a right to transfer or otherwise dispose of his property to another citizen of Bangladesh. This right is available to every citizen of Bangladesh under the Constitution and such right can only be restricted or abridged by way for promulgation of law. In the present case the restriction said to have been imposed to the petitioner belonging to the Marwari Community; not by any law but by an administrative order having not the force of law. The learned Counsel cited the case of Chitta Ranjan Sutar Vs. Secretary Judicial Department, Govt. of East Pakistan Building, Dacca, District Registrar, Bakerganj reported in 17 DLR page 451 wherein it was held: 

 9. In the above said case it was held that restrictions imposed to the rights of the citizen in contravention of the fundamental right being discriminatory guaranteed under the Constitution and in presence of those restrictions the registering authority refused to accept the sale deed for registration was found to have been made without any lawful authority and of no legal effect. In the instant case we have already found that the restriction imposed are not by way of any promulgation of law but it is done by way of administrative order. Here we are not to find out the reasonableness or otherwise of the order, we are to see only whether this order has the sanction of law. The order having imposed restriction on the right of the petitioner to transfer or otherwise to dispose of his property to another also on the right of the citizen of Bangladesh to acquire property is discriminatory and also violative of the fundamental right guaranteed under the Constitution and the equality clause provided under Article 31. The learned Assistant Attorney General then submits that against the refusal of the prayer for registration of the sale deed the other remedy by way of filing appeal to the District Registrar was open and, therefore, the petitioner can not seek relief before this Court in its writ jurisdiction as an alternative remedy. Mr. S. R. Pal submits that as against the refusal to accept the sale deed for registration, there is no provision for appeal before the Registrar. It is further submitted that since the impugned order has been passed by the respondent No. 3 refusing to accept the sale deed for registration on the basis of the Administrative order issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs, there is no efficacious remedy other than the remedy herein prayed for in this petition and, therefore, the maintainability of the writ petition cannot be questioned by the Respondents. 

 10. Regard being had to the facts and circumstances of the case and the law involved therein, we hereby declare that the endorsement dated 16.7.1991 made on the sale deed refusing to admit the document for registration and the connected Memo No. 320(19)-Swa: Ma (Ni-1) dated 10.6.1975 issued by the Ministry of Home Affairs have been made without lawful authority and is of no legal effect. The respondent No. 3 is hereby directed to accept the kabala for registration and thereafter register the same in accordance with the provision of the Registration Act, if it is not otherwise barred by law.
